what: The score is the fixed-position insertion-distance increase minus a bounded credit for distance from the depot. The credit ranges from 0.30 to 0.45 of the depot distance, increasing when the candidate consumes a larger fraction of the route's remaining capacity. It runs in O(len(route)) time to compute current load and uses O(1) extra space.
why: Pure cheapest insertion can repeatedly postpone remote customers whose eventual service may require another long depot trip. The radial credit gives such customers moderate urgency while retaining insertion detour as the dominant geometric signal. The capacity-normalized adjustment weakly favors good packing and customers likely to become infeasible later; normalization makes it applicable across the substantially different capacities and demand scales in the examples. The bounded coefficients prevent radial urgency from overwhelming a clearly bad cross-cluster insertion. This is only a construction heuristic: it has no admissibility or remaining-cost interpretation, performs no multi-customer lookahead, and may be less effective when radial distance poorly represents route structure. Its coefficients require evaluation on held-out instances, and no empirical improvement is claimed.
